target: Widespread co-ignimbrite fallout, Pedrazzi Unit G and explicitly correlated distal beds.

sites.name: TUNU2013
sites.reference: Smith et al. 2020, polar ice-core results, Fig. 4, Table 2 and Methods
sites.inspection: Glass chemistry identifies a TBJ occurrence. The meltwater sample does not resolve the eruptive phase or give bulk ash mass per unit ground area. No Unit G thickness or bound enters the fit. 14–15 identified particles over a 3.3 × 3.3 cm nominal cross-section give 1.29–1.38 recovered particles/cm². The sample spans ~2.5 years. Recovery fraction, full particle volumes, phase share and deposition/preservation transfer are unknown.

sites.name: DSDP 67-499-1R-CC
sites.reference: Schindlbeck et al. 2018 Table 3 C1; DSDP Leg 67 Site 499 p. 284
sites.inspection: 67-499-1R-CC 0–20 cm is the analysed core-catcher interval, at 0.59 mbsf. Shipboard log records void and muddy ash; rotary drilling and possible lateral sediment transport break both endpoint transfers. Possible overlap with D19-M05; never count its map reading twice.

sites.name: V15-26
sites.reference: Kutterolf 2008a Table 1 C1 and section 4.2.6; Bowles et al. 1973
sites.inspection: Published C1 correlation to this named legacy core. The regional 1–12 cm bed-size description includes many other eruptions. No C1-specific paired contacts, thickness or calibrated pod transfer recovered. Dull Fig 9 marks have no station keys.

sites.name: Offshore Osa Peninsula
sites.reference: Dull 2019 Fig 9; Schindlbeck et al. 2016 southern CAVA survey
sites.inspection: Question mark is attached to the >1 numeral. No matching Costa Rican station or glass analysis in Dull supplementary Table S2b. Preserve the possible >1 cm reading for the far SE search; uncertain event attribution and position cannot justify a principal lower bound.
